newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori vows to hold line on Peruvian wages.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori vows to hold line on Peruvian wages.

text.p: Peru's government, insisting on fiscal discipline, will hold down public sector wages indefinitely as a way of keeping the budget in balance, President Alberto Fujimori said.

Fujimori admitted wages were not keeping up with inflation but that the only way to raise them would be to print money. He has come under pressure from teachers and other civil servants to boost salaries.
"We must recognise that we are lagging in the area of remunerations," he said Sunday night in an interview on local Panamericana Television.

"But I ask you, is there any other way? No. We have looked for some other way, and in the end we realise that in this case, we would have to go back to the printing press. What we are doing is a very serious job of maintaining a balanced budget," said Fujimori.
Public sector wages have fallen about six percent against inflation since the last wage increase in the second half of 1996, he said.
Strong economic growth has so far brought little benefit to salaries in Peru. The minimum wage stands at about $170 a month
